description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census.

Data::Dump is a pure-Perl renderer of a value: it walks a structure and prints
the perl source that would rebuild it.  That makes its t/ files a MIRROR of
PCL's value model â every divergence below is PCL's representation showing
through, not a Data::Dump bug â and it makes them unusually good diagnostics.

BOARD ROWS (perl passes every one; reproduce with
`tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Data-Dump-1.25-0 t/<file>`):

  dump.t 35, 36     `bless \$sv` marks the REFERENT blessed, not the reference:
                    perl `bless(do{\(my $o = [])}, "foo")`,
                    PCL  `bless(do{\(my $o = bless([, "foo"))}, "foo")`
                    â that half is #1511 B and is NOT this task.
  scalar.t 1,2,3    3 rows, whole file FAIL 0/3 (perl 3/0)
  scalar-obj.t 1    a blessed SCALAR
  ref.t 2           the `\do{my $fix}` cycle-fixup form
  regexp.t 1        qr// literals inside a structure
  tied.t 1,2        a tied hash / array, with Data::Dump's `# tied MyTie` note
  quote-unicode.t 5 the `("\x{FFF}\x{100FF}" x 30)` repeat form
  filtered.t 24     `Bar=HASH(0xc)` â a filtered object's stringification
  dd.t              FAIL 0/0 (perl 1/0), no error reported: the file produced
                    no TAP in the census run and TAP on a re-run â re-measure
                    before diagnosing (it may be the load flake the same census
                    found in Algorithm-Diff, now handled by the scoreboard's
                    signal-killed retry)
  glob.t            NOT this task â it dies "Undefined subroutine
                    &IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX called" (#1574)

HOW TO WORK IT: each row prints the whole expected source string in its
`expected` column of baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv, so the diff is readable
without running anything.  Take ONE (scalar.t is the smallest, 3 rows, and it
is a FAIL 0/3 so something dies early), probe the value it dumps against perl,
and split this task at the first real mechanism you find â like #1571, this is
a bundle by population, not one bug.


=== MEASURED + CLOSED (s523b, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-20) -- the bundle has dissolved ===
One-file runs on the tree (main 6cf75804 + s523b): scalar.t 3/0, scalar-obj.t 3/0, ref.t 2/0, regexp.t 1/0, tied.t 4/0, filtered.t 41/0, dd.t 1/0, dump.t 38/0 -- every row this task listed PASSES (fixed by earlier batches; the board file had already dropped them -- only two Data-Dump rows were left in baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv at launch).  The ONE remaining row of this task, quote-unicode.t 5 (`("\x{FFF}\x{100FF}" x 30)`, PCL `x 60`), is #932 (capture variables are not dynamically scoped): Data::Dump::str computes `length($_)/length($1)` AFTER `quote($1)`, and quote's `s/([^\040-\176])/.../eg` leaves $1 at one character in PCL where perl restores the caller's $1 on return.  Probe scratch/s523b/p2/qu.pl (perl / tree): the regex itself agrees (`/^(.{2,5}?)\1*\z/s` matches with length($1)=2 on both); only the count after the call differs.  Row re-caused #932 by edit.  Nothing in PCL names Data::Dump (rule 9a).
subject: Data::Dump renders PCL values differently from perl (9 board rows over 8 files) â a pure-Perl MIRROR of the value model: blessed scalars, cycle fixups, qr//, tied containers, the x-repeat form
